title: Matthew Chapter 19 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Matthew chapter 19 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Matthew Chapter 19 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Matthew Chapter 19.

questions.question: In Matthew 19, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Pharisees asked about putting away wives
Disciples said it is not good to marry
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus departed from Galilee
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:1 states that Jesus departed from Galilee and came into the coasts of Judaea beyond Jordan, which is the earliest event mentioned.

questions.question: Where did Jesus go after finishing his sayings according to Matthew 19:1?
options: Into the coasts of Judaea beyond Jordan
questions.correctAnswer: Into the coasts of Judaea beyond Jordan
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:1 states Jesus departed from Galilee and came into the coasts of Judaea beyond Jordan.

questions.question: Who followed Jesus and were healed according to Matthew 19:2?
questions.correctAnswer: Great multitudes
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:2 states that great multitudes followed Jesus and he healed them there.

questions.question: What question did the Pharisees ask Jesus in Matthew 19:3?
options: Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife for every cause?
Can a man marry more than one wife?
Should we pay taxes to Caesar?
Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?
questions.correctAnswer: Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife for every cause?
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:3 records that the Pharisees asked Jesus if it is lawful for a man to put away his wife for every cause.

questions.question: According to Jesus in Matthew 19:4, how were humans made at the beginning?
questions.correctAnswer: Male and female
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:4 states Jesus answered that he who made them at the beginning made them male and female.

questions.question: What did Jesus say a man shall do for his wife in Matthew 19:5?
options: Leave father and mother and cleave to his wife
Stay with his father and mother always
questions.correctAnswer: Leave father and mother and cleave to his wife
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:5 quotes that for this cause a man shall leave father and mother and shall cleave to his wife.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about the two becoming one flesh in Matthew 19:6?
options: They are no more twain, but one flesh
questions.correctAnswer: They are no more twain, but one flesh
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:6 states that wherefore they are no more two but one flesh, and what God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.

questions.question: Why did Moses command to give a writing of divorcement according to Jesus in Matthew 19:8?
options: Because of the hardness of your hearts
questions.correctAnswer: Because of the hardness of your hearts
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:8 states Moses allowed putting away wives because of the hardness of the people's hearts.

questions.question: In Matthew 19:9, what does Jesus say about a man who puts away his wife except for fornication and marries another?
questions.correctAnswer: He committeth adultery
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:9 states that whoever puts away his wife except for fornication and marries another commits adultery.

questions.question: What did the disciples say to Jesus about marriage in Matthew 19:10?
options: If the case of the man be so with his wife, it is not good to marry
It is good to marry many wives
questions.correctAnswer: If the case of the man be so with his wife, it is not good to marry
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:10 records the disciples saying that if the case of the man be so with his wife, it is not good to marry.

questions.question: According to Matthew 19:6, what should not be done to what God hath joined together?
questions.correctAnswer: Put asunder
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:6 states that what God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus healed the great multitudes who followed him in Judaea beyond Jordan.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:2 states that great multitudes followed Jesus and he healed them there.

questions.question: True or False: The Pharisees came to Jesus to tempt him with a question about putting away a wife for every cause.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:3 says the Pharisees came to Jesus tempting him, asking if it is lawful to put away a wife for every cause.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus said that Moses commanded divorce because it was God's original plan.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:8 states Moses allowed divorce because of hardness of hearts, but from the beginning it was not so.

questions.question: True or False: According to Matthew 19, Jesus said whosoever marries a put-away woman commits adultery.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:9 says whoso marrieth her which is put away doth commit adultery.

medium.title: Matthew Chapter 19 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Matthew Chapter 19 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who cannot receive the saying that Jesus spoke in Matthew 19:11?
questions.correctAnswer: All men
questions.explanation: Jesus states that 'All men cannot receive this saying, save they to whom it is given.' (Matthew 19:11)

questions.question: What does Matthew 19:12 suggest about eunuchs?
options: They are all born that way
questions.correctAnswer: Some are made by men
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:12 describes that 'there are some eunuchs, which were made eunuchs of men.'

questions.question: What did the disciples do when little children were brought to Jesus?
questions.correctAnswer: Rebuked them
questions.explanation: The disciples rebuked those who brought the children to Jesus (Matthew 19:13).

questions.question: What promise does Matthew 19:14 make concerning little children?
options: They belong to the kingdom of heaven
questions.correctAnswer: They belong to the kingdom of heaven
questions.explanation: Jesus says, 'for of such is the kingdom of heaven.' (Matthew 19:14)

questions.question: What did Jesus do to the little children?
options: He laid his hands on them
questions.correctAnswer: He laid his hands on them
questions.explanation: Jesus laid his hands on the children before departing (Matthew 19:15).

questions.question: What did the young man ask Jesus in Matthew 19:16?
options: What shall I do for eternal life?
questions.correctAnswer: What shall I do for eternal life?
questions.explanation: The young man asked, 'Good Master, what good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life?' (Matthew 19:16)

questions.question: What does Matthew 19:17 instruct for entering life?
questions.correctAnswer: Keep the commandments
questions.explanation: Jesus instructs, 'but if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.' (Matthew 19:17)

questions.question: Which commandments did Jesus mention in Matthew 19:18?
questions.correctAnswer: Do not murder
questions.explanation: Jesus lists, 'Thou shalt do no murder, Thou shalt not commit adultery...' (Matthew 19:18).

questions.question: What does Matthew 19:19 say about loving your neighbor?
questions.correctAnswer: It is a commandment
questions.explanation: Jesus commands, 'Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.' (Matthew 19:19).

questions.question: What did the young man claim in Matthew 19:20?
options: He had kept all the commandments
questions.correctAnswer: He had kept all the commandments
questions.explanation: The young man said, 'All these things have I kept from my youth up.' (Matthew 19:20).

questions.question: What important lesson can be drawn from Jesus' response to the young man's question?
options: The necessity of obedience to commandments
questions.correctAnswer: The necessity of obedience to commandments
questions.explanation: Jesus emphasizes the importance of keeping the commandments to enter life (Matthew 19:17).

questions.question: What connection is made between the treatment of children and the kingdom of heaven?
options: Children are a model for entry into the kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: Children are a model for entry into the kingdom
questions.explanation: Jesus states that 'for of such is the kingdom of heaven,' highlighting that children exemplify the qualities needed to enter (Matthew 19:14).

questions.question: True or False: Jesus rebuked the disciples for bringing the children to him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jesus did not rebuke the disciples; He instead told them to allow the children to come to Him (Matthew 19:14).

questions.question: True or False: Jesus stated that no one is good except God.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jesus said, 'there is none good but one, that is, God' (Matthew 19:17).

questions.question: True or False: The young man was unsure about his adherence to the commandments.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The young man claimed he had kept all the commandments from his youth (Matthew 19:20).

hard.title: Matthew Chapter 19 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Matthew Chapter 19.

questions.question: According to Jesus in Matthew 19:21, what must the young man do to be perfect?
options: Go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor, and follow me
Keep all the commandments from his youth
questions.correctAnswer: Go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor, and follow me
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:21 records Jesus saying, 'If thou wilt be perfect, go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me.'

questions.question: Why did the young man in Matthew 19:22 go away sorrowful?
options: Because he was rejected by Jesus
Because he was afraid of the Pharisees
questions.correctAnswer: Because he had great possessions
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:22 states, 'But when the young man heard that saying, he went away sorrowful: for he had great possessions,' explaining his sorrow.

questions.question: What does Jesus say about a rich man entering the kingdom of heaven in Matthew 19:23?
options: A rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven
A rich man will be the first to enter
A rich man has no need to enter
A rich man can enter by giving offerings
questions.correctAnswer: A rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven
questions.explanation: In Matthew 19:23, Jesus says, 'Verily I say unto you, That a rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven.'

questions.question: What metaphor does Jesus use in Matthew 19:24 to describe the difficulty for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God?
options: It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle
It is like finding a pearl of great price
It is like climbing a steep mountain
It is like crossing a raging river
questions.correctAnswer: It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:24 uses the metaphor: 'It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.'

questions.question: In Matthew 19:26, what does Jesus say about what is possible with God?
options: With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible
Only some things are possible with God
Nothing is impossible for men alone
questions.correctAnswer: With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:26 states, 'With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible,' highlighting divine omnipotence.

questions.question: What promise does Jesus give to those who have forsaken all and followed Him, according to Matthew 19:28?
options: They shall sit upon twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel
They will receive riches in this life
They shall be healed and prosper
questions.correctAnswer: They shall sit upon twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:28 says that those who have followed Jesus will 'sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel' in the regeneration.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'teleios' in Matthew 19:21 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Perfect or mature
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'teleios' (τελειος) in Matthew 19:21 means 'perfect' or 'mature,' referring to spiritual completeness.

questions.question: Which literary device is illustrated by Jesus' statement in Matthew 19:30, 'many that are first shall be last; and the last shall be first'?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasmus
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:30 uses chiasmus, a literary device where elements are presented and then repeated in reverse order to emphasize a concept.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is echoed by Jesus’ teaching on marriage in Matthew 19:4-6?
questions.correctAnswer: Genesis 2:24
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:4-6 cites Genesis 2:24 about a man leaving father and mother to cleave to his wife, establishing the biblical basis for marriage.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects with the theme of forsaking all for Christ’s sake as stated in Matthew 19:29?
questions.explanation: Mark 10:29-30 parallels Matthew 19:29 by affirming that those who forsake family or possessions for Jesus’ name receive a hundredfold and eternal life.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Jesus’ conversation with the young rich man in Matthew 19:16?
options: Jesus debates with the Pharisees about divorce
Jesus delivers the Sermon on the Mount
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus blesses little children
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:13-15 shows Jesus blessing little children just before the young man approaches Him in verse 16.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'eye of the needle' metaphor in Matthew 19:24 when considering historical context?
options: It emphasizes the impossibility of a rich man entering heaven
It refers to a known narrow gate in Jerusalem
It symbolizes the fine thread of a true disciple
It means the camel must shed its wealth
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes the impossibility of a rich man entering heaven
questions.explanation: Historically, the metaphor in Matthew 19:24 stresses the near impossibility (hyperbolic language) for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God due to attachment to wealth.

questions.question: How does Matthew 19:26 reflect the theme of divine omnipotence compared to human limitation?
options: It contrasts human impossibility with God’s unlimited power
It suggests humans can achieve anything alone
It denies any possibility of salvation
It claims only the wealthy can be saved
questions.correctAnswer: It contrasts human impossibility with God’s unlimited power
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:26 explains that what is impossible for men is possible with God, emphasizing divine omnipotence over human limitation.

questions.question: In Matthew 19:28, what is the 'regeneration' referring to in its theological context?
options: The future renewal of all things at Christ’s second coming
The birth of Jesus in Bethlehem
questions.correctAnswer: The future renewal of all things at Christ’s second coming
questions.explanation: The term 'regeneration' in Matthew 19:28 refers to the eschatological renewal, often associated with Christ’s return and the establishment of His kingdom.

questions.question: True or False: According to Matthew 19:29, those who forsake possessions for Jesus’ name shall inherit everlasting life.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:29 states explicitly that those who forsake houses, family, or lands for Jesus’ name shall inherit everlasting life.

theological.title: Matthew Chapter 19 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Matthew Chapter 19 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 19:6 teach about the nature of marriage?
options: Marriage unites two individuals into one flesh, ordained by God and not to be separated by man
Marriage is a temporary covenant that can be dissolved by mutual consent
Marriage is primarily a social contract subject to cultural norms
Marriage is only valid if sanctioned by religious authorities
questions.correctAnswer: Marriage unites two individuals into one flesh, ordained by God and not to be separated by man
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:6 states, 'Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder,' teaching that marriage is a divine union not to be broken by human decision.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin and divine accommodation is taught in Matthew 19:8?
options: Moses permitted divorce due to hardness of heart, but it was not God's original intent
Divorce was God's ideal law from the beginning
Human sin does not affect divine law on marriage
Divorce is never allowed under any circumstances
questions.correctAnswer: Moses permitted divorce due to hardness of heart, but it was not God's original intent
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:8 explains that 'Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so,' showing divine accommodation to human sinfulness.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 19:26 teach about salvation?
options: Salvation is impossible by human effort but possible with God
Salvation is guaranteed to all regardless of faith
Salvation depends solely on human moral achievement
Only the wealthy can be saved
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is impossible by human effort but possible with God
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:26 states, 'With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible,' emphasizing that salvation depends on divine power, not human ability.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Matthew 19:17 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness
questions.explanation: Jesus says in Matthew 19:17, 'there is none good but one, that is, God,' highlighting God's unique holiness and moral perfection.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly demonstrated in Matthew 19:14?
questions.correctAnswer: Grace
questions.explanation: In Matthew 19:14, Jesus welcomes children despite disciples' rebuke, showing God's grace and inclusive love toward the humble and weak.

questions.question: How does Matthew 19:28 connect to the broader biblical theme of eschatological judgment?
options: It affirms the future reign of Christ and the role of the twelve apostles in judging Israel
It denies any future judgment and focuses only on present life
It suggests human judges replace divine judgment
It limits judgment to earthly courts
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms the future reign of Christ and the role of the twelve apostles in judging Israel
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:28 speaks of the Son of man sitting on his throne in glory and the apostles judging the twelve tribes, aligning with eschatological themes in Daniel 7 and Revelation.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Matthew 19:23-24 make regarding wealth and salvation?
options: It echoes Old Testament warnings about reliance on wealth over God
It teaches that wealth guarantees divine favor
It claims wealth is irrelevant to spiritual life
It encourages accumulation of riches as a sign of blessing
questions.correctAnswer: It echoes Old Testament warnings about reliance on wealth over God
questions.explanation: Jesus' teaching that it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom (Matthew 19:23-24) reflects Old Testament prophetic critique of idolatry of wealth (e.g., Amos 6:4-6).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 19:9 and Matthew 19:11 teach about marriage and sanctification?
options: Marriage is to be lifelong except in cases of sexual immorality, and not all can accept this high calling
Divorce is permitted for any reason and all must marry
Everyone is required to remain single for spiritual purity
questions.correctAnswer: Marriage is to be lifelong except in cases of sexual immorality, and not all can accept this high calling
questions.explanation: Verse 9 permits divorce only for fornication, while verse 11 acknowledges that not all can accept this demanding teaching, indicating varied callings to marriage or singleness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 19:12 and Matthew 19:14 teach about the kingdom of heaven?
options: The kingdom is open to those who choose celibacy for its sake and to humble children
Only the physically strong enter the kingdom
The kingdom excludes those who abstain from marriage
Children must prove their righteousness to enter
questions.correctAnswer: The kingdom is open to those who choose celibacy for its sake and to humble children
questions.explanation: Verse 12 explains some choose eunuch status for the kingdom's sake, while verse 14 affirms that children belong to the kingdom, showing its accessibility to the humble and self-denying.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 19:28 and Matthew 19:29 teach about discipleship and eternal rewards?
options: Those who follow Christ faithfully will reign with Him and receive manifold blessings in the age to come
Discipleship guarantees earthly riches but no eternal reward
Faithfulness is irrelevant to eternal inheritance
Rewards depend solely on works without faith
questions.correctAnswer: Those who follow Christ faithfully will reign with Him and receive manifold blessings in the age to come
questions.explanation: Verse 28 promises apostles will sit on thrones judging Israel in the regeneration, and verse 29 promises a hundredfold and eternal life for those who forsake for Christ's name.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Jesus' teaching in Matthew 19:16-22 is a call to legalism and wealth renunciation for salvation. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Salvation requires obedience to commandments and willingness to sacrifice earthly wealth, not legalistic works-righteousness
Salvation is earned by selling all possessions
Jesus condemns all rich people as unsalvageable
The passage teaches salvation by works alone
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation requires obedience to commandments and willingness to sacrifice earthly wealth, not legalistic works-righteousness
questions.explanation: Jesus points to keeping commandments (v.17-19) and calls the young man to sacrificial discipleship (v.21), emphasizing heart obedience over legalism or blanket condemnation of wealth.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 19:3 teach about the Pharisees' understanding of marriage and human sin?
options: The Pharisees tested Jesus on divorce, reflecting a legalistic and permissive stance toward marital dissolution
The Pharisees upheld God's original intent for marriage without exception
They rejected any form of divorce under any circumstance
They taught that marriage was irrelevant to the Law
questions.correctAnswer: The Pharisees tested Jesus on divorce, reflecting a legalistic and permissive stance toward marital dissolution
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:3 shows Pharisees tempting Jesus with a question about divorce 'for every cause,' indicating their permissive interpretation of Mosaic law.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Jesus' response to the disciples' amazement about salvation in Matthew 19:26?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Jesus declares salvation is impossible with men but possible with God (Matthew 19:26), demonstrating God's sovereign power over salvation.

questions.question: How does Matthew 19:10-12 prepare for the New Testament teaching on spiritual gifts and callings?
options: It acknowledges diverse vocations including celibacy for kingdom purposes
It mandates marriage for all believers
It denies any special calling beyond marriage
It restricts celibacy to those forced by others
questions.correctAnswer: It acknowledges diverse vocations including celibacy for kingdom purposes
questions.explanation: Verses 10-12 describe eunuchs born, made, or chosen for the kingdom, recognizing varied God-given callings, paralleling Paul’s teaching on spiritual gifts and callings (1 Corinthians 7).

questions.question: What theological truth is taught in Matthew 19:29 about discipleship and reward?
options: Those who sacrifice for Christ’s name will receive manifold blessings and eternal life
Physical sacrifices have no spiritual reward
questions.correctAnswer: Those who sacrifice for Christ’s name will receive manifold blessings and eternal life
questions.explanation: Verse 29 promises 'an hundredfold, and shall inherit everlasting life' to those who forsake for Christ's sake, teaching the doctrine of sacrificial discipleship and divine reward.
